Our Story

A Family Estate in the Middle of Westernport Bay

Mandalaye Park Estate sits on French Island, in the middle of Westernport Bay — 61 km southeast of Melbourne, yet a world away from it. The suites sit in the grounds of the historic homestead, surrounded by gardens, paddocks and the estate's magnificent oak trees.

French Island is home to around 100 residents, and roughly 70% of it is crown land, state and national parks. There is no mains water or mains electricity — island life runs on solar power, generators and rainwater, at a pace set by the ferry timetable and the seasons.

"Country life as it used to be — and Mandalaye Park is your place within it."

Koalas, echidnas and peacocks roam free here, and the only cars on the island belong to the locals.

French Island

One of Victoria's Last Untouched Islands

The island covers 170 square kilometres of wetlands, salt marshes, coastal heaths and swamps, with over 480 species of indigenous plants — White Mangroves, Marsh Saltbush, Creeping Rush and Salt Lawrencia among them, many rare or threatened.

There are no foxes, kangaroos, possums or wombats on the island. Its only school, Perseverance Primary, had six primary-age children enrolled in 2019 — island life at its quietest and most genuine.

How to Get Here
— i.

The Chicory Kiln

Chicory — an early form of coffee — was the island's main income for over 70 years, from the late 1800s to the middle of last century. Mandalaye Park's kiln, built in the early 1900s, still holds some artefacts, and a family of barn owls now nests in its roof.

— ii.

Wildlife, Up Close

Koalas in the treetops, echidnas in the grass and peacocks on the lawn — the island's animals roam free, and Mandalaye Park's 142 acres are home to many of them.

— iii.

The McLeod Prison Farm

Opened on 17 July 1916 as a tent village, the McLeod prison farm ran as a self-sustaining farm until it closed in 1975. It is now privately owned — one more layer of the island's remarkable history.

Getting There

The Journey Is Part of It

1

Train or Drive to Stony Point

Metro trains run to Frankston, with a diesel service on to Stony Point station for a standard metro ticket — some trains connect with the ferry. Free parking is available at the Stony Point Foreshore.

2

Ferry to Tankerton Jetty

Western Port Ferries run daily from Stony Point (about 15 minutes) and from Cowes on Phillip Island (about 20 minutes) to Tankerton Jetty. The ferry is passenger-only — bring your bike aboard for the island's 40+ km of gravel tracks.

3

Bringing a Vehicle

The Spirit of French Island barge runs a vehicular ferry from Corinella to the island's barge landing, carrying two standard-size cars or a larger truck.
